finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The code does not involve any user input or external command execution. The signal handling is controlled internally within the program.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported sink is kill(getppid(), SIGINT) on line 32. kill() is a system call that sends a signal to a process; it does not execute an external command string. The source of the PID is getppid(), which returns the parent process ID of the current process and is an internal value, not influenced by any untrusted input. Therefore there is no path from untrusted data to a command execution primitive, and OS Command Injection cannot occur here.

finding.title: Race Condition
finding.trigger: Race condition between fork() and pause()
finding.assumptions: The code does not handle potential race conditions between the fork() and pause() calls. An attacker could potentially exploit this to send a signal before the parent process is ready to handle it.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the signal handler setup (lines 16-18) and confirmed it occurs before the fork (line 25). The child process sends SIGINT only after a 1‑second sleep (lines 31-33). The parent calls pause() after the fork (line 36). Since the handler is installed before the fork, any SIGINT sent by the child will be caught immediately, regardless of whether pause() has been called. If the signal were delivered before pause(), pause() would return immediately upon the pending signal. Thus there is no exploitable race condition between fork() and pause().

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Raising SIGINT to test if the handler has been reset
finding.assumptions: The code does not involve any user input or external command execution. The signal handling is controlled internally within the program.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any untrusted data source feeding into the raise(SIGINT) call. The code contains no user input, file reads, network data, environment variables, or external parameters that could influence the signal value. The signal value SIGINT is a compile‑time constant. Therefore, there is no path from an untrusted source to the sink, and the reported OS Command Injection claim is invalid.
